options.content: Two parents and their children
options.rationale: Correct: it is the smallest family unit.

options.content: Parents, children and other relatives such as grandparents, aunts and uncles
options.rationale: That describes an extended family.

options.content: One parent living with one or more children after a divorce or a death
options.rationale: That describes a single-parent family.

options.content: Children living without adults, with an older sibling as the head of the household
options.rationale: That describes a child-headed family.

explanation: A nuclear family is two parents and their children. Extended families include other relatives.

stem: Who is the **vatete** (ubabakazi) in a family?

options.content: The father's sister
options.rationale: Correct: the paternal aunt, who often advises young women.

options.content: The mother's brother, who often supports his sister's children in many families
options.rationale: That is the sekuru or umalume (maternal uncle).

options.content: The father's elder brother, who has authority in the paternal family
options.rationale: That is the babamukuru.

options.content: The mother's mother, who cares for grandchildren and shares family history
options.rationale: That is a grandmother.

explanation: Vatete (Shona) and ubabakazi (Ndebele) mean the father's sister.

stem: Which family is an example of a child-headed family?

options.content: A mother and father with two children living in a flat in Harare
options.rationale: That is a nuclear family.

options.content: A widow living with her children, her mother and her brother in a rural homestead
options.rationale: That is an extended family.

options.content: A man and woman joined by remarriage, with children from their earlier relationships
options.rationale: That is a blended family.

options.content: Three siblings living alone, with the eldest aged sixteen looking after the others
options.rationale: Correct: no adult lives with them.

explanation: A child-headed family is one in which children, usually led by the eldest, live without an adult.

stem: Which statement best explains why belonging to a family is important?

options.content: It guarantees that a person will never face any difficulty or sorrow in life
options.rationale: No family can guarantee this.

options.content: It allows a person to avoid all duties to relatives and to the community
options.rationale: Belonging brings duties as well as support.

options.content: It ensures that every member will always agree with the decisions of the elders
options.rationale: Family life involves respect, but members do not always agree.

options.content: It gives a person identity, security, education and religious life
options.rationale: Correct: the family is the first community.

explanation: A family gives identity (name, totem), security (care in need), education (values) and religious life (ceremonies).

stem: In Indigenous Religion, who is regarded as part of the family?

options.content: Only the people who share the same house today and eat from one pot
options.rationale: The family includes relatives who do not live in the home.

options.content: Only the people who share the same church or place of worship
options.rationale: Family is based on kinship, not on a place of worship.

options.content: The living members and the ancestors
options.rationale: Correct: the ancestors remain members of the family.

options.content: Only the first-born son and the people whom he has chosen to live with
options.rationale: The family includes many members, not only the eldest son.

explanation: In IR the family includes the living and the ancestors, who guide and protect it.

stem: Thandeka's father has died. Her umalume pays part of her school fees, her ubabakazi advises her about the future and her grandmother cares for her little brother. What does this show?

options.content: The mother has no role in the family because other relatives have taken over
options.rationale: The scenario does not say that the mother has no role.

options.content: Responsibility is shared among members of an extended family
options.rationale: Correct: relatives each take a role in caring for the children.

options.content: A nuclear family can meet every need of its members without help from outside
options.rationale: The example shows that other relatives are needed.

options.content: Only the paternal relatives are expected to help when a family loses its father
options.rationale: Both maternal and paternal relatives help in the example.

explanation: In an extended family different relatives share responsibilities for support, guidance and care.
hints: Look at who helps, and how many different relatives are involved.

stem: Which pair correctly matches a religion with a family teaching mentioned in this topic?

options.content: Judaism: kindness to parents (Ephesians 6:1-3)
options.rationale: Ephesians is a book of the Christian New Testament, not a Jewish text.

options.content: Islam: kindness to parents (Qur'an 17:23)
options.rationale: Correct: the Qur'an teaches kindness to parents.

options.content: Christianity: kindness to parents (Qur'an 17:23)
options.rationale: The Qur'an is the Muslim scripture.

options.content: Indigenous Religion: kindness to parents (Exodus 20:12)
options.rationale: Exodus is part of the Torah and the Bible, not an IR source.

explanation: Judaism and Christianity both cite Exodus 20:12 on honouring parents; Christians also cite Ephesians 6:1-3; Muslims cite Qur'an 17:23.
hints: Check which scripture belongs to each religion.

stem: Which statement is the fairest comparison of nuclear and extended families?

options.content: Nuclear families are always happier than extended families because they are smaller
options.rationale: Size does not decide happiness.

options.content: Each has strengths and difficulties, and neither is the only correct form
options.rationale: Correct: families vary, and a balanced answer does not rank them.

options.content: Extended families always give better care because there are more people in them
options.rationale: More people do not always mean better care; conflicts can arise.

options.content: Only extended families can pass on values to children and take part in religious life
options.rationale: Nuclear families also pass on values.

explanation: Extended families share work and care but can face conflict; nuclear families have privacy but fewer helpers. A balanced answer does not rank them.

stem: An extended family includes relatives such as grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins.
explanation: True. An extended family includes relatives beyond the parents and children.

stem: A single-parent family is one in which both parents live with their children.
explanation: False. A single-parent family has one parent living with the children.

stem: Match each kinship term with its meaning.
explanation: Vatete/ubabakazi: paternal aunt. Sekuru/umalume: maternal uncle. Babamukuru: father's elder brother.

stem: What type of family is formed when two partners with children from earlier relationships join as one household?
explanation: A **blended family** joins two families after remarriage.

points.description: Nuclear
Extended or single-parent
Child-headed, blended or polygamous

explanation: One mark for each type named.

stem: Describe the roles of grandparents and of aunts and uncles in an extended family.

points.description: Grandparents share wisdom and stories and care for grandchildren
Grandparents are respected as a link with the past and the ancestors
Aunts and uncles advise and guide young people
Aunts and uncles help in key events such as marriage and give support when parents cannot

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Grandparents share wisdom and stories, care for grandchildren and are respected as a link with the past. Aunts and uncles advise and guide young people, take part in events such as marriage and give support when parents cannot.

explanation: One mark for each accurate point.
hints: Give two points for each group of relatives.

stem: Explain why the extended family is important in Zimbabwean society.

points.description: Shared responsibility for care of children and old people
Developed: when parents are sick or have died, relatives can step in so that children do not go without care
Passing on values and identity
Developed: grandparents, aunts and uncles teach respect, names, totems and history to the young
Economic and emotional support
Developed: relatives share money, food or school fees in hard times and support one another at funerals and weddings

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The extended family shares responsibility for care. When parents are sick or have died, relatives step in, so children do not go without care. It also passes on values and identity, because grandparents, aunts and uncles teach respect, names, totems and family history. It gives economic and emotional support too, because relatives share money, food or school fees in hard times and stand together at funerals and weddings.

hints: Give three reasons: care, values and identity, and support.

stem:
**Source A** — an extract from a fictional school magazine article, Gweru, 2026 (invented for this question)

> After our parents died, my older sister Rudo, who is seventeen, took charge of the house. She cooks, makes sure we go to school and signs our school forms. Our aunt visits every month to bring food and talk to us, and a neighbour helps us to plant our field. Rudo says: 'We are still a family, even without grown-ups in the house.'

Study Source A and answer the questions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which type of family is described in Source A?

options.content: Nuclear, with both parents living in the house with the children
options.rationale: The parents have died.

options.content: Blended, with children from earlier relationships living together
options.rationale: No remarriage is mentioned.

options.content: Child-headed
options.rationale: Correct: children live without an adult, led by Rudo.

options.content: Polygamous, with a husband and more than one wife in the household
options.rationale: No husband or wives are mentioned.

parts.explanation: The children live without adults and the eldest is in charge.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State **three** things Rudo does for her brothers and sisters.

points.description: Cooks for them
Makes sure they go to school
Signs their school forms

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: She cooks, makes sure they go to school and signs their school forms.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **two** ways in which the wider community and relatives help the family in Source A.

points.description: The aunt visits monthly with food and gives advice and support
A neighbour helps plant the field, so the family can grow food

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The aunt brings food every month and talks to the children, which supports and guides them. A neighbour helps to plant their field, which helps the family to grow food.

explanation: The source shows a child-headed family supported by an aunt and a neighbour.
hints: In (c), say what the help is and what it achieves.

stem: Nokuthula says: "The extended family is the best kind of family because it shares responsibility." Themba says: "Smaller families can give children more attention."

points.description: Shared care for children, the sick and the elderly
Support in hard times, such as money for fees or help with funerals

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Care for children, the sick and the elderly is shared among relatives. Relatives also give support in hard times, such as help with school fees and funerals.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give **two** difficulties that extended families can face.

points.description: Disagreements over money, land or decisions
Limited space and resources in the home, or less privacy

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There can be disagreements over money, land or decisions. There can also be limited space and resources, with less privacy in a crowded home.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Assess whether the extended family is better for children than the nuclear family.

points.description: For extended: shared care, more role models, identity and values
For nuclear: more attention and privacy, fewer conflicts over resources
A supported judgement, such as that both can succeed depending on the care and love in them

levels.descriptor: Considers both views with developed reasons and a supported judgement.
Both views, with limited development or an unsupported judgement.
One view developed or both only listed.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: An extended family offers shared care, many role models and a strong sense of identity and values. However, a nuclear family may give children more individual attention and privacy and avoid conflicts over resources. Both can succeed or fail, depending on the love, discipline and support children receive, so neither is better in every case.

explanation: A balanced answer weighs both family types and avoids ranking.
hints: Give the strengths of each type before your own judgement.
